record: Study 3b settings: small and fine-grained categories with count models, and sentiment direction. Fixed before any 3b result was computed.
fixed_by: Khant Phyo Wai (with Claude). Khant asked for this on 2026-10-13 because the minimum-size rule of Study 3 made the #MeToo control and COVID-19 audiobooks untestable, and they want to study smaller, easy-to-miss events and negative as well as positive sentiment.
relation_to_study3: Study 3 stays the primary, fixed analysis and is reported as run. Study 3b is a second analysis added after Study 3 results were seen (disclosed below). It keeps every Study 3 setting except those changed here.
unchanged_from_study3: shift definitions (with addenda d, g, h, i)
month 0 and the effect windows (0..+2 primary, 0..+5 secondary)
the event-study fit window (24 months ending at month -7)
the three positive controls and their months
missing, partial and closure months (addenda b, e)

levels.value_level: taxonomy v3 theme values (work_theme_value: work, theme, weight). Interest shifts at value level are detected with the Study 3 rules on value-level Wikipedia and GDELT series, using the same quality screens.

no_size_threshold: There is no minimum-size rule. A test is run whenever the model below can be fitted: the category has a nonzero weighted checkout in at least 12 of the 24 fit months in at least one format. Tests with fewer than 5 expected weighted checkouts over the primary window are reported separately as too sparse.

demand.counts: Y_{c,f,t} = sum over works of theme weight x checkouts (narrow and middle: work_theme strength; value: work_theme_value weight); exposure N_{f,t} = all checkouts in format f, month t
demand.formats: the Seattle formats are modelled jointly in one model per test (missing format-months simply drop out); per-format effects are reported as secondary. LibriVox is analysed separately with its own exposure (all LibriVox views).

count_event_study.model: quasi-Poisson GLM on the fit months: log E[Y_{c,f,t}] = log N_{f,t} + alpha_f + beta_f * t + sum_k gamma_k 1[month(t) = k] (format-specific level and trend, shared month-of-year effects); dispersion phi estimated by Pearson chi-square / residual df
count_event_study.expected: mu_{c,f,t} predicted for the effect window from the fitted model
count_event_study.effect: tau = log( sum over formats and window months of Y / sum of mu ); per-format effects the same within one format
count_event_study.standardised_gap: z = ( log(sum Y) - log(sum mu) ) / sqrt( phi / sum mu ), so that small and large categories are comparable

inference.placebo_categories: the same model at the same month 0 for every other category at the same level that has no interest shift start in months -6..+6 and does not share its parent; one-sided p = rank of the treated z among treated and placebo z values / (number of placebos + 1)
inference.placebo_years: the same category and calendar months in every other year from 2017 without a shift in that window; share of placebo z at or above the treated z
inference.detected: one-sided p < 0.05 for a single test; BH q < 0.10 within each level across all main tests

positive_controls.rule: run first; pass = tau > 0 with one-sided placebo-category p < 0.05 in the joint Seattle model
controls: George Floyd / BLM: Race and racism (narrow), 2020-06
positive_controls.value_level_controls: also reported at the value level for the values inside these nodes (descriptive, not part of the pass rule)

power.method: multiply the observed Y of placebo categories by (1 + L) in months 0..+2 after random placebo start months and rerun the count event study
power.size_bands: quartiles of the expected weighted checkouts over the primary window (sum of mu), computed per level
power.minimum_detectable_effect: smallest lift detected in at least 80% of draws, per level and size band

all_shifts.set: quality-ok main-set shifts (labelled, not seasonal) at the narrow, middle and value levels, from 2017-01
all_shifts.pooled: mean tau by source, level and duration class with a bootstrap clustered by category
all_shifts.carry_over: the Study 3 carry-over regression with tau from this model as the outcome

sentiment.question: Does negative as well as positive news sentiment carry over into demand, and does emotional intensity matter?
features: delta tone (mean of the first 4 weeks minus the 26-week median)
tests: each feature added to the carry-over regression on its own
comparison with 200 placebo windows per category, two-sided
sentiment.source: GDELT tone only (2017-01 to 2021-06 until the backfill, then rerun to the end with the same settings)
sentiment.emotions: named emotions (fear, anger, sadness and others from GDELT GCAM) are not part of this record; they need a separate record if the data are obtained

disclosures: Study 3 results were known when this record was fixed: positive controls (race and racism passed; COVID-19 epidemics ebook +0.27, p 0.115; #MeToo untestable by the size rule), power (80% detection only at about +50%), all-shift results (no single shift after BH; sustained shifts +0.08 to +0.11 log share pooled) and tone (no tone feature beat its placebo).
Study 4 forecasting results were known (interest did not improve one-month-ahead forecasts).
The sizes of the control categories (median weighted checkouts) were known.
deviations: changes after this date go to DEVIATIONS.md (Study 3b section) and prereg/addenda_3b/
